entries.reason: The reference bundle registers a 2-argument Coalesce macro while desktop has no such macro: CQL Coalesce is a variadic Python UDF (CQL-08 removed the arity cap). This is the one place the browser has a macro desktop lacks. Removes when a native variadic Coalesce ships in the C++ extension and the TS macro is deleted.
entries.approved_by: Joel Montavon, 2026-11-24: build the test infrastructure first; not a fix-everything pass

entries.reason: SetVariable's desktop body calls the Python-only UDF _setvariable_impl, which the browser does not have, so the generator cannot emit it. Translator variable plumbing used only by desktop parameter paths; no translated test or measure SQL on the browser contract emits it today. Removed by porting the UDF to the C++ extension (then regenerate the reference bundle).

Both app bundles predate the reference: they still register CAST-based ToDate/ToDateTime/ToTime macros (the ToDate DATE-vs-VARCHAR drift already fixed in the cleanroom) and lack statements added since. Fix: import the reference module from both apps and re-run their Playwright suites.

Desktop wraps a Python UDF in a same-name macro; the browser contract runs the native C++ namesake. Both match the official expectation, but the declared type differs: desktop DECIMAL(2,0) vs native INTEGER (predecessor/successor) and typed UNION vs VARCHAR (High/LowBoundary). Values agree.

Desktop interval UDFs are Python and serialise interval JSON with spaces, unquoted numbers and Time bounds without the 'T' prefix; the native C++ mirror emits compact JSON with quoted numbers and 'T' bounds. Both match the official expectation (the comparators parse the JSON).

Desktop evaluates High/LowBoundary through the Python UDF (a null precision means the default precision, CQL-10); the browser contract runs the C++ mirror, which returns NULL for a null precision. Fix: port the null-precision default into the native boundary helpers and rebuild the bundles.

Fail on BOTH surfaces against the official corpus (first seen at f724ee4, re-triaged at 0a8f7d3): desktop conformance defects, not parity gaps. In flight with the fhir4ds test fixes (Joel, 2026-11-24). CoalesceMoreThanFiveArgs left this list when FHIR4-44 made it a translation error.

In flight in the fhir4ds lane. Dev landed the strict Boolean comparison in the official CQL gate (FHIR4-33) before the engine changes that satisfy it. Seven of the nine first registered no longer reproduce after FHIR4-34/38/39/40 and were removed from this entry. These two still fail on the desktop surface: properly includes / properly in over Time bounds with second-vs-millisecond precision (the AMUX-171 remaining gap). Removes when that fix merges (this registration then goes stale and must be deleted).

Tier C: every population boolean equals desktop, but two 'which encounter' columns (Encounter with Malnutrition Risk Screening or with Dietitian Referral; ... At Risk or with Dietitian Referral) name a DIFFERENT single encounter for 7 patients: the SQL picks one row among ties and row order is unspecified across engines, so desktop and duckdb-wasm pick different members of the same qualifying set. Removes when the lowering orders the pick deterministically.

Tie order in `sort by periodStart`. Patient a46db6aa-5016-4111-bc4e-a31156c87ec6 has two atomoxetine MedicationRequests authored on 2026-01-02 (209-day and 1-day supply), so the `rolloutIntervals` aggregate depends on the order of two tied rows: desktop keeps source order (209-day first, the order the reference engine's stable sort gives and the fixture expects) and answers [[2026-07-30, 2026-07-30], [2026-01-02, 2026-07-29]]; real duckdb-wasm processes the 1-day request first and answers [[2026-01-03, 2026-07-30], [2026-01-02, 2026-01-02]]. Column 'ADHD Medications Taken on IPSD or During Continuation and Maintenance Phase'. Removed by a deterministic tie-break in the translated sort (WP-6).

The native highBoundary/lowBoundary disagree with the official expectation while the Python core passes (typed inputs, since WP-3): decimals that arrive in exponent notation (9.5e2) lose the mantissa precision the spec says counts (highBoundary(0) gives 951, not 955), and the DateTime millisecond boundary of an offset value is wrong (@2014-01-01T08:05-05:00.highBoundary(17) gives ...T08:59:59.999-12:00, not ...T08:00:59.999-12:00). Identical on the x86 and the wasm build, so every browser has it. Removed by a native fix in extensions/fhirpath plus an x86 and a wasm bundle rebuild; this gate flips to STALE then.

Native unescape('json') leaves \uXXXX and \" escapes in place ('\\u0041B'.unescape('json') stays \\u0041B instead of AB) while the Python core passes. Identical on the x86 and the wasm build, so every browser has it. Removed by a native fix plus an x86 and a wasm bundle rebuild.
